text:
acme-pm: Hey, we rotated our API key via Vault last night and ~10% of our serverless workers in eu-central started getting 401s around 02:12 UTC. Other regions are fine.

alice_support: Sorry for the hassle — can you share a sample request id and a 401 response body?

acme-pm: req=ea3f2b11, response: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"token not valid"} — same client code, same deployment job.

ben_oncall: Noted. Did the vault-agent rollout complete on those eu-central VMs? Any sidecar logs?

acme-pm: We use the vault sidecar to inject env vars at startup. The sidecar log shows rotation event: "vault-bot: rotated secret secret/data/acme/prod/apikey -> version 4" — but our app logs still show old key in env.

vault-bot: rotated secret secret/data/acme/prod/apikey -> version 4 (automated rotation)

carol_infra: Hm — serverless workers are on Windows Server images in eu-central for historical reasons. Do those processes support SIGHUP-style reloads? If you rely on env var hot-reload the platform may not propagate.

acme-pm: Oh. Our init script expects vault-agent to write to file and then os.Signal(SIGHUP) to reload. Windows doesn't support SIGHUP so servicectl sends a custom event. It worked previously.

alice_support: Two angles: 1) app didn't pick up new env so it's presenting old API key -> 401 because key revoked; 2) or KMS envelope rewrap failed for some requests causing decryption to return stale value. Can you paste the vault-agent sidecar log lines around rotation for one affected instance?

acme-pm: pasted snippet:
```
2026-03-16T02:11:58Z vault-agent: checking for rotation
2026-03-16T02:12:01Z vault-bot: rotated secret secret/data/acme/prod/apikey -> version 4
2026-03-16T02:12:02Z vault-agent: wrote /var/secrets/acme_apikey (mode 0400)
2026-03-16T02:12:02Z app: no reload handler, will continue running with previous env
```

ben_oncall: That line is the smoking gun: vault-agent wrote new file but app didn't re-exec or reload. On Windows the typical pattern is to restart the service. Can you try a graceful restart of one worker and confirm it picks the new key?

acme-pm: Trying a restart now on one affected instance (eu-03-worker-17)...

acme-pm: Restarted, retested req ea3f2b11 -> 200 OK. Session shows tokens accepted. So restarting fixes it. But we can't restart hundreds during business hours. Any zero-downtime approaches?

dan_cs: For customer-facing guidance: recommend configuring the app to watch the secret file and perform runtime reload (e.g., SignalServer on Windows using service manager), or use sidecar that proxies the credential instead of baking env vars.

carol_infra: Also check KMS Key policy in eu-central. I spotted intermittent errors in the control plane logs where envelope decryption returned AccessDenied for the vault server role for a subset of requests during the rotation window. That would cause vault-agent to fail to unwrap new ciphertext and fallback to old value. If some sidecars wrote stale values and others wrote new ones, that would create the 10% pattern.

alice_support: Can you grep vault server logs for AccessDenied entries around 02:12? If present we need to update the KMS key policy to allow vault service principal for eu-central alias.

acme-pm: Found these in vault logs:
```
2026-03-16T02:12:01Z kms: Decrypt failed: AccessDenied: User arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/vault-eu not authorized to use key alias/awskms-eu-acme
2026-03-16T02:12:01Z vault: rotation aborted for instance eu-03-worker-41, fell back to previous version
```

ben_oncall: That confirms mixed cause: (A) KMS policy denied some unwrapping -> some agents couldn't write new ciphertext; (B) windows workers didn't reload env -> some agents wrote new key but app retained old. Net result: partial 401s.

alice_support: Action items for short term: 1) Restart affected Windows workers (or set an automated rolling restart window). 2) Patch KMS key policy to include vault-eu role. 3) Apply a one-off vault rewrap to ensure all instances end up with same version.

carol_infra: I'll open the KMS policy change PR — minimal policy addition: allow kms:Decrypt for arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/vault-eu on key alias/awskms-eu-acme. Example snippet:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/vault-eu"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

acme-pm: Thanks, PR looks good. After we restarted ~30 windows workers and carol applied the policy, errors dropped to near-zero. We then triggered a manual rewrap; vault-agent logs show all instances wrote version 5.

vault-bot: rotated secret secret/data/acme/prod/apikey -> version 5 (manual rewrap)

acme-pm: Confirmed: all eu instances now 200.

dan_cs: Follow-ups: (1) Recommend switching from env-injection to a sidecar proxy or a credential fetch with runtime watch on Windows. (2) We can add a health-check that compares app key against vault's current version and emits a warning if mismatch. (3) We'll document KMS key-policy checklist in the postmortem.

alice_support: I'll create a support ticket with reproduction steps and include the logs and the PR link. acme-pm, do you want us to coordinate a low-impact rolling restart during EU off-hours?

acme-pm: Yes please — coordinate with me for a 2am CET window. Appreciate the quick triage.

ben_oncall: Scheduling with infra for 02:00 CET, automated restart job for Windows workers, and adding a small script to watch secrets file and call `sc control app-service param` to trigger reload as a short-term mitigation.

carol_infra: Adding postmortem checklist entry: "Verify KMS key policies for all regional vault roles before enabling rotation", and a howto for Windows service reload patterns.

alice_support: Ticket created SUP-2026-3421 and assigned to eng-infra + cust-success. Closing thread, will update when scheduled restarts complete. :thumbsup:
